method: Androguard 4.1.4 static manifest parsing + Android Build Tools 35.0.0 apksigner signature verification. APKs were not installed or executed. All twelve APKs were uploaded to the deployed Linux API and their private reports deleted after verification. Malicious inputs stayed in original password-protected research archives locally and were decrypted in memory for static upload only.
limitations: Twelve selected samples demonstrate integration behavior, not sensitivity, specificity or detection accuracy.
Five malicious APKs represent three historical research campaigns/families; each exact digest matches its primary research IOC.
Five upstream open-source releases are provenance controls, not guaranteed-safe applications.
Two intentionally insecure training controls are separate from the five documented malicious specimens.
Valid signatures establish file signer identity, not publisher legitimacy or safety.
Declared permissions are capabilities; grants, actual behavior, remote code, DEX behavior and signing lineage are not assessed.
APK binaries, private session tokens, certificate subjects and embedded personal strings are excluded from publication.
